I recently purchased a bike from TVS – Raj 2 Wheelers LLP, and unfortunately, the overall experience was extremely disappointing.

Despite informing the showroom in advance before leaving my place, the bike was not arranged on time, and I ended up receiving the delivery almost 2 hours late. What made the situation worse was the complete lack of coordination and product knowledge among the staff. There was no single point of contact, and most employees seemed unaware of the process or responsibilities.

Only Manager Manish and a bank representative, Shantanu, appeared to have any meaningful understanding of the product and the delivery status. The rest of the staff were mostly roaming around and were of no help, forcing me to repeatedly chase different people for basic updates.

The behavior of the reception staff was particularly unprofessional. They were more focused on their computers and showed little to no interest in assisting customers. When asked for help, their responses and expressions were dismissive and uncomfortable, making the customer feel unwelcome and unimportant.

Buying a new bike is a special moment for any customer, but this showroom managed to turn it into a frustrating and disrespectful experience. I strongly feel the staff needs proper training in customer service, ownership, and communication.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this showroom to anyone looking for a smooth and respectful buying experience.

featured_reviews.name: Akhil Vishnu
featured_reviews.review_text: Chor Bazaar is one of Mumbai's most iconic and storied markets, nestled in the heart of South Mumbai. Located on Mutton Street, near Bhendi Bazaar in Grant Road, this legendary flea market has been a treasure trove for antique collectors, vintage enthusiasts, and bargain hunters for over 150 years. Chor Bazaar's history dates back to the 19th century when it was originally known as *Shor Bazaar*, meaning "noisy market" in Hindi, owing to its bustling and loud atmosphere filled with vendors hawking their wares. The British, unable to pronounce "Shor" correctly, transformed it into *Chor Bazaar*, translating to "Thieves' Market" – a name that stuck, partly due to tales of stolen goods finding their way into the market. One popular anecdote associates the name with Queen Victoria's visit to Bombay (now Mumbai), where some of her belongings, including a violin, went missing from her ship and were later found for sale in this very market – adding to the "thieves' market" lore. Chor Bazaar wasn't always synonymous with stolen goods; it's now predominantly a hub for *antiques*, *vintage items*, and *second-hand goods*. Visitors can unearth rare artifacts like old bronze statues, colonial-era furniture, gramophones, vintage cameras, retro Bollywood posters, typewriters, and even automobile spare parts. The market has distinct areas like the Automobile Section for spare parts and an Antique Section housing vintage treasures. Jumma Market is a special early morning market on Fridays (4:30 AM-7 AM) in Dedh Gully, attracting bargain hunters for items like branded shoes at discounted prices. Bargaining is mandatory at Chor Bazaar; prices are fluid and haggling is an integral part of the shopping experience. Bollywood prop hunters and film production houses often source unique items here, adding to its cinematic allure. The atmosphere is characterized by narrow lanes and crowded shops where vendors double as storytellers sharing histories of their wares. Located in a predominantly Muslim neighborhood, 90% of the area reflects local Islamic culture, leading to Friday closures except for the early Jumma Market. Timings generally stretch from 11 AM to 7:30 PM (Saturday-Thursday); Fridays see closure except the Jumma Market early morning slot. Accessibility is convenient with Grant Road railway station nearby, reachable via Mumbai's public transport network. Visitors should dress modestly respecting local norms in this Muslim-majority area. Crowds can get chaotic; patrons are advised to watch their belongings amid risks like pickpocketing. Proximity to landmarks like Haji Ali Dargah and Mahalakshmi Temple makes it accessible for those exploring Mumbai's spiritual and cultural hubs. Chor Bazaar embodies Mumbai's cultural fusion and recycling ethos – where yesterday's discards become today's treasures. It's a sensory overload in the best possible way, appealing to those seeking retro gems and bargain adventures. The name "Chor Bazaar" itself evokes curiosity, mixing intrigue with the thrill of treasure hunts. Dealers range from those selling serious antiques to purveyors of quirky collectibles reflecting Mumbai's layered past.
